newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swap - Regrade widen on bullish jet.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swap - Regrade widen on bullish jet.

text.p: Singapore gas oil swaps moved lower on weaker overnight crudes, with the regrade seen widening as jet gains momentum, rising faster than gas oil, traders and brokers said on Friday.
July gasoil swaps were quoted at $22.30/$22.40 per barrel, August at $22.70/$22.90, down about 25 cents from Thursday, brokers said.
Traders said prices were weaker due to overnight crude losses.
But jet/gas oil bids for July edged about 10 cents higher from its previous day's quotes, indicative that outright spreads levels have firmed.
Brokers said the regrade had widened on the back of firmer jet cash prices.
On Thursday, a 130,000 barrel cargo of jet fuel for lifting in July was traded at $24.65 per barrel free-on-board (fob), up 45 cents from Wednesday's traded level.
Traders also said jet demand from Indonesia is picking up.
Indonesia is expected to buy three million barrels for August delivery, up about one million from its normal monthly import.
But firmer regrade quotes may not last long, said traders.
They said gas oil prices were expected to catch up when Chinese demand returns in August after the Hong Kong handover.
Rumours were also heard that a local trader, long on July paper positions may surface to support physical prices.
Fuel oil swaps were little moved despite crude losses.
Traders said prices had fallen by at least $3 per tonne on Thursday and is now consolidating.
They were uncertain if prices had fallen due to weaker fundamentals or due to a handful of players who were pricing the market.
The traders said demand is expected to rise in August as Indonesia is expected to import some cargoes with two of their refineries undergo maintenance shutdown.
July was last quoted at $98.50/$99.75 per tonne.
